items.title: Hadi Awang: Muslims less involved in corruption than non-Muslims due to faith
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has claimed that Muslims are less involved in corruption compared to non-Muslims, arguing that Islamic institutions such as Tabung Haji are singled out for scrutiny specifically because of their religious branding. “Muslims involved in corruption are not as many as non-Muslims, because they are guarded by faith and belief that there is sin before Allah,” he said. Hadi also contended that enforcement against corruption in Malaysia has been selective and unjust.

items.title: Sick projects fall to 36 nationwide, says Ahmad Maslan
items.summary: MELAKA: The number of sick projects under the Works Ministry and Public Works Department (PWD) nationwide has fallen to 36, or 4.13 per cent, from 53, or 6.81 per cent, in June last year. Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said only one sick project had been identified in Melaka. He said the ministry had set a key performance indicator to reduce the proportion of sick projects nationwide to 3 per cent by November.

items.title: UK media skewered for 'hounding' black academic
items.summary: THE British press is once again in the spotlight for its methods, this time over accusations that its full-throttle coverage of plagiarism allegations against the Cambridge academic Jason Arday led to his untimely death. Arday, who was appointed in a blaze of publicity in 2023 as the youngest-ever black professor to Cambridge University, was found dead last Friday, aged 41, after weeks of excoriating media reports. "I believe the vicious media campaign drove him to his death," MP Diane Abbott, the first black woman elected to the UK parliament, told the vigil.

items.title: AI adoption can cut road maintenance costs, says Nanta
items.summary: Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the innovative approach is crucial to balancing the government's financial constraints while upgrading the country's road infrastructure. He said investment in improving road infrastructure and safety is not merely physical spending, but a critical government measure to save road users' lives. On road accident figures, Nanta said statistics released by the Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research (Miros) are worrying.

items.title: Proton Saga driver cleared, released over fatal Jalan Sultan Ismail crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Proton Saga driver involved in the fatal Jalan Sultan Ismail crash has been released and will not be charged over the incident, the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) confirmed today. The driver was initially detained alongside the 43-year-old Immigration Department lorry driver to assist investigations into the crash, which claimed the lives of three members of the same family. Asked whether the Proton Saga driver would face charges, Masri said there was no basis to charge him as the Immigration Department lorry was believed to have run a red light.

items.title: Muhyiddin trial: Contractor says gave Bersatu RM1 as he was told ex-PM ‘helped’ win project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — Businessman Lian Tan Chuan today said that his Bumiputera construction company Nepturis Sdn Bhd had in 2022 given RM1 million as a “reward” to Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia, as he was told that its party president and then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin had “helped” the company secure a RM141 million project under the government’s Jana Wibawa programme. In comparison to smaller sums of RM5,000 and RM10,000 donations sought by Bersatu member Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad for social work, Lian said the RM1 million donation amount to Bersatu requested by Malaysia’s Bumiputera contractors’ association president Datuk Azman Yusoff was a “very big” amount. Lian previously said that he had agreed to Azman’s request to pay the RM1 million to Bersatu after Nepturis got the project.

items.title: Sarawak: Haze prompts two-day school closure in 6 areas
items.summary: KUCHING: The Sarawak Education Department has ordered all schools under its jurisdiction in Kuching, Padawan, Serian, Bau, Lundu and Samarahan to close with immediate effect today and tomorrow due to haze affecting air quality in the areas. The department said that schools would conduct Home-Based Teaching and Learning during the closure to ensure students could continue their studies. The statement said that updates on the closure duration and school reopenings would be announced through the department's official channels and District Education Offices.

items.title: Palapes cadet death case transferred to Johor Baru High Court
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: The case involving the death of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Reserve Officers' Training Unit (Palapes) cadet Syamsul Haris Shamsudin has been transferred from the Sessions Court to the Johor Bahru High Court for trial. High Court judge Atan Mustaffa Yussof Ahmad allowed an application by deputy public prosecutor Nor Afiqah Musa, who submitted that the case was of significant public interest. The application followed a directive by Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar after lawyer Datuk Naran Singh, who represents Syamsul Haris' family, applied for the case to be heard by the High Court.

items.title: Firefighters quell 'numerous flare-ups' in Belgian wildfire
items.summary: SOURBRODT: Firefighters wrestled "numerous flare-ups" under control overnight in a final push to quell Belgium's massive High Fens wildfire, officials said Thursday, pushing into a seventh day despite "dangerous" conditions on site. Strong winds buffeted southeastern Belgium Wednesday night, with gusts uprooting trees and a "mini-tornado" partially destroying a house in Bullange just outside the nature reserve, the town's mayor told local media. An update from local authorities said fire crews worked all-night "but were limited by the dangerous terrain: lack of visibility, trees downed by the storm, mud and hard-to-access trails."

items.title: JS-SEZ draws 1,436 investment inquiries, Johor eyes high-value spillovers [WATCH]
items.summary: SINGAPORE: The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) has attracted 1,436 investment inquiries since January last year, as Johor seeks to turn growing investor interest into high-value projects, quality jobs and opportunities for local businesses. Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said 43 of the investment prospects were referred by Singapore's Economic Development Board (EDB) and Enterprise Singapore. This reflects the role of Singapore's investment agencies in channelling potential investors into the zone.

items.title: MH89 take-off aborted at Narita over engine issue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines flight MH89 from Tokyo Narita International Aiport to Kuala Lumpur aborted take-off today following a technical issue involving one of its engines. Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), in a statement, said all passengers and crew were safe. "The flight was subsequently cancelled and the aircraft is undergoing a thorough technical inspection.

items.title: Police rescue 17 Jordanian children from trafficking syndicate in KL
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A three-month-old baby was among 17 Jordanian children rescued by police following raids on a child trafficking and exploitation syndicate in Bukit Bintang and Chow Kit here yesterday. Five of the suspects, however, failed to produce valid travel documents. Initial police investigations revealed that the syndicate members had entered Malaysia legally on 90-day social visit passes.

items.title: [UPDATED] Woman injured in Jalan Sultan Ismail crash that killed husband, two children stable
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 55-year-old woman whose husband and two children were killed in yesterday's Jalan Sultan Ismail crash is in stable condition. Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Muhammed Hasbullah Ali said the woman was still receiving treatment in the yellow zone at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL). "Her condition is currently stable.

items.title: AUKU to be abolished entirely this year, says PM
items.summary: KLANG: Legislation to abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU) is expected to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat this year, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. "Yesterday, during the cabinet meeting, I said I wanted to abolish it entirely," he said in his speech at a Temu Anwar session with students today. He said greater freedom would not mean students would never make mistakes, but said this should not be used as a reason to retain restrictions on them.

items.title: Thai, Myanmar military chiefs meet as post-coup thaw progresses
items.summary: BANGKOK: Myanmar's military chief met Thursday with Thailand's top general in Bangkok in his first foreign trip since assuming the role, as his coup-staging armed forces shake off their pariah status. After the elections, Min Aung Hlaing – who led the coup as armed forces chief – took over as civilian president, handing the office of military leader to staunch loyalist Ye Win Oo. The previous high-level military talks were held in Myanmar in 2023, two years after the coup, when Min Aung Hlaing was head of the military.

items.title: Malaysian Airlines confirms MH89 Tokyo-KL flight cancelled due to technical issue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — Malaysia Airlines has confirmed that flight MH89 from Tokyo Narita International Airport to Kuala Lumpur was cancelled today after the aircraft aborted its take-off due to a technical issue involving one of its engines. In a statement issued here, Malaysia Airlines apologised for the disruption and confirmed that all affected passengers are being assisted with alternative travel arrangements. Affected travellers will be accommodated on the next available flights to Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Developer withdraws Kota Damansara data centre application after public raises concerns, says Ramanan
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 20 — The proposed data centre project in Kota Damansara is off the table for now, after the developer withdrew its planning permission application to the Petaling Jaya City Council. Sungai Buloh Member of Parliament Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said he received the latest update on the matter from the local council. Ramanan, who is also the Human Resources Minister, said this latest development shows that the voices and concerns of people, when raised through the proper channels, can yield tangible results.

items.title: Malaysian police rescue 17 Jordanian children from lucrative KL begging syndicate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — Police have dismantled a suspected foreign child trafficking syndicate that allegedly forced 17 Jordanian minors into begging across the city’s busiest tourist and commercial districts. Seven of these took place on public walkways while six targeted residential premises used by the group. Police believe the group is part of an organised syndicate masterminded by Jordanian nationals who entered Malaysia legally on 90-day social visit passes.

items.title: [UPDATED] Beacon lights, sirens no licence to beat red lights, says Bukit Aman traffic chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Flashing beacon lights and blaring sirens are no licence to run a red light, even in an emergency. Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said drivers of enforcement and emergency vehicles must ensure an intersection is safe before proceeding. Hasbullah said even vehicles responding to emergencies must exercise caution before entering an intersection against a red light.

items.title: Anwar: Govt fast‑tracking drafting of new e‑commerce Bill
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the move was important to ensure the e-commerce ecosystem develops in an orderly manner while providing greater convenience and protection for all stakeholders, including young people and new entrepreneurs. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the new legislation should be expedited to meet the needs of industry players while providing greater security and protection for those involved in digital commerce. Anwar said the growth of technology and e-commerce platforms had created new opportunities for young people to venture into business, particularly those with limited capital and experience.

items.title: AmBank sees limited direct Middle East impact, keeps SMEs and exporters on watch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The direct impact of Middle East disruptions on AmBank Group's borrowers remains limited, with no defaults linked to the conflict so far, its chief said. However, shipment delays and rising input costs are putting some exporters and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) under closer scrutiny, AMMB Holdings Bhd group chief executive officer Jamie Ling said. Ling said the group had seen some borrowers affected by inconsistent shipments, particularly exporters to Asia, as supply chain disruptions build up.

items.title: Batu Pahat set for advanced manufacturing push, RM3.78m allocated
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: Johor is positioning Batu Pahat for high-value manufacturing investment through a proposed Advanced Manufacturing Park (AMP), with the aim of creating better-paying jobs and broader economic opportunities for locals. He said the plan would also strengthen logistics connectivity between Batu Pahat and the North-South Expressway-West Coast Expressway (NSE-WCE) corridor. "Through JETP, the state government is emphasising development that leverages Batu Pahat's strengths and potential, including the proposed development of an AMP to attract high-value manufacturing industries, talent development in Industry 4.0, automation and robotics, as well as strengthening logistics networks connecting Batu Pahat with the NSE-WCE corridor."

items.title: Anwar rules out full GST return, citing cost-of-living concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ruled out the Goods and Services Tax (GST) as Malaysia’s primary tax pillar, maintaining that a broad-based consumption tax would disproportionately burden the nation’s low-income groups. Speaking to local media following the launch of the TikTok Shop Summit 2026 today, Anwar emphasised that any tax reform must align with the government’s commitment to social equity. Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan is currently spearheading the feasibility study of this hybrid model.

items.title: Teo Nie Ching urges platforms to fully comply with Risk Mitigation Code to curb online fraud
items.summary: KLANG, Aug 20 — The government hopes that all online platforms will fully comply with the Risk Mitigation Code, which came into force on June 1 under the Online Safety Act 2025 (Act 866), to strengthen measures against fraudulent and harmful online content. She said the existing legal framework was sufficient to address online crimes and security issues, including through amendments to the Communications and Multimedia Act (CMA), the Online Security Act and the Cybecrime Act. Meanwhile, she said the increase in online purchases had resulted in higher demand for last-mile delivery vehicles, making the use of greener vehicles important in reducing environmental pollution.

items.title: Onn Hafiz urges Johoreans to fill stadium for JDT's world-record bid
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi has called on Johoreans to fill the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium this Friday as Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) chase a new world record for the longest unbeaten home league run. Onn Hafiz said JDT had equalled the record last season and now had the opportunity to make history on home soil. "Let's fill the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium and witness another historic moment for Johor together.

items.title: Jualan Ihsan Rahmah 9.9 to go online on Sept 9
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will hold the Jualan Ihsan Rahmah 9.9 online sale on Sept 9 in conjunction with Malaysia Day celebrations. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the sale, which will be held online for the first time, would give people nationwide an opportunity to purchase essential goods at affordable prices. "I want to align this with the Jualan Ihsan Rahmah 9.9 online sale," he said in his speech at the TikTok Shop Summit Malaysia 2026 here today.

items.title: MyBorderPass glitch hits KSAB, travellers told to use manual counters
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Travellers using the bus and motorcycle lanes at the Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB) here were forced to use manual immigration counters today after the MyBorderPass application experienced a system disruption. The Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) said the disruption affected MyBorderPass access at both entry and exit lanes for buses and motorcycles at the Immigration, Customs and Quarantine (ICQ) Complex in Tanjung Kupang. It follows a nationwide immigration system outage, which affected 114 entry points earlier this year, disrupting clearance systems including MyBorderPass QR facilities and forcing manual processing at major entry points, including Johor's land checkpoints.

items.title: Not just raw exports: Malaysia demands tech transfer from REE investors
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 20 — Investors eyeing Malaysia’s rare earth elements (REE) industry must be prepared to share their technology and commit to the entire value chain if they wish to secure a foothold in the country, according to Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. The minister said that Malaysia is moving away from the model of merely exporting raw resources. “For us to obtain the full benefits from rare earths, we must establish activities not only in the upstream sector, where we export, but also across the upstream, midstream and downstream sectors,” Johari said.

items.title: 2 students plead guilty over insulting TikTok comments targeting disabled girl
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: Two 17-year-old students pleaded guilty in the magistrate's court here today to posting insulting comments on TikTok targeting a disabled teenage girl. They were charged with using insulting words in comments posted on a TikTok video belonging to the 17-year-old victim. The victim spotted the offensive comments on her TikTok account.

items.title: Sepang police probe repeated nail‑scattering incidents at Cybersouth flyover that endangers motorists
items.summary: SEPANG, Aug 20 — Police are investigating and attempting to locate an individual believed to be responsible for repeatedly scattering nails along the left off-ramp of the Cybersouth flyover, an act that poses a serious threat to road users. Sepang police chief ACP Norhizam Bahaman said police received a report regarding the incident on July 15 and are continuing to monitor the area to identify the individual responsible. The convoy travelled 14 kilometres from IPD Sepang to SJKC Dengkil.

items.title: Immigration busts alleged foreign‑run prostitution ring in KL
items.summary: He said that, in addition to the Bangladeshi and Thai couple, authorities also detained a local man who was acting as the premises’ caretaker, along with 23 other foreign nationals. “The foreign nationals detained comprised three men from Myanmar, three Bangladeshi women, 14 Indonesian women, two Vietnamese women and a Myanmar woman, aged between 18 and 35,” he said in a statement today. “The syndicate operated by using residential and commercial premises to conduct illicit activities involving foreign women as sex workers,” he said.

items.title: Anwar: Govt open to improving SST, adopting some GST components
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will not consider the basic essence of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) because the tax is broad-based and levied on the public, including the poorest groups. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said if necessary, improvements to the implementation of the Sales and Service Tax (SST) could be made by incorporating certain components of the GST. "I am not prepared to consider the basic essence of GST because it is still a broad-based tax that imposes tax on every single citizen, including the poorest of the people.

items.title: Iran slams Trump's economic pressure plan as more 'failed policies'
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Thursday dismissed US President Donald Trump's economic punishment plan for Teheran as a continuation of "failed policies", which he said would bring Washington "further defeat." Meanwhile, Iran's military has begun signalling a shift from retaliation to offence, which analysts say could reflect Teheran's belief it holds leverage to advance its demands and break the stalemate. Last week, a deputy commander of Iran's Revolutionary Guards indicated that Teheran was revising its military doctrine to give "offensive operations" strategic priority.

items.title: Hunt continues for trio behind RM1.7m Genting jewellery heist
items.summary: KUANTAN: Police are on the trail of three masked men who fled with jewellery worth RM1.7 million after robbing a goldsmith shop at SkyAvenue, Genting Highlands, Bentong, on Aug 17. Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob remained tight-lipped about the investigation, saying police were still gathering details about the trio. "The Genting Highlands robbery is still under investigation.....we are still gathering information and clues related to the incident," he told reporters at the Alor Akar police logistics complex here today.

items.title: Is your home protected against EV fire? Here’s what Malaysian Insurers have to say
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — The recent fire involving an electric vehicle (EV) in Alam Damai, Cheras has raised questions about insurance coverage if something goes wrong while charging an EV at home. If an EV or its charging equipment causes a fire, is your home actually covered? “So fire is a fire.

items.title: Malaysia's One China policy unchanged, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has reaffirmed Malaysia's long-standing stance on the One China policy, saying it has remained consistent since the administration of Tun Abdul Razak Hussein. Anwar said Malaysia's position was not new, but one that had been upheld continuously since the time of the second prime minister. He added that Malaysia respected China's position but believed a peaceful resolution remained the best course.

items.title: Anwar: PH-BN Melaka election talks to be handled by election committees
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Any discussions on cooperation between PH and BN for the upcoming Melaka election will be handled by the respective coalitions' election committees, said PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. "We have PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail leading the negotiations," he told reporters after officiating the TikTok Shop Summit Malaysia 2026 here today. Earlier, Saifuddin did not rule out meeting Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to discuss cooperation ahead of the state election.

items.title: SARI@KRT programme to help 1,400 domestic violence survivors nationwide rebuild lives, says Nancy Shukri
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) has launched the Santun Kasih Pemandiri@Keganasan Rumah Tangga (SARI@KRT) programme to assist 1,400 domestic violence survivors nationwide in rebuilding their lives. Its minister, Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri, said the programme targets at least 100 participants in each state, with a focus on strengthening psychosocial support and legal assistance, as well as empowering women affected by domestic violence economically. She said misunderstandings and communication problems remained the leading causes, accounting for 1,967 cases, followed by drug abuse with 444 cases and financial stress with 378 cases.

items.title: Anwar orders expedited drafting of e-commerce Bill
items.summary: Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the move was aimed at improving the ease of doing business and regulatory oversight in the sector, in line with the rapid growth of digital businesses. He said the government was also open to views from industry players on ways to improve the ecosystem. Anwar said improvements to the e-commerce sector must be accompanied by appropriate regulation to prevent the digital space from being abused.

items.title: Kyiv's desperate vendors persevere outside obliterated flea market
items.summary: ON the scorching asphalt besides what was once a bustling Kyiv flea market, vendors were trying to sell the remains of their stock, ravaged by a Russian missile strike. Moscow destroyed the popular Pochaina site in Petrivka, north of the Ukrainian capital in a major attack last month – the third on the market since Russia invaded in February 2022. A similar scene plays out every day at the central Lukyanivka market.

items.title: Ahmad Maslan: Negri Sembilan political alignment may extend to Melaka
items.summary: AYER KEROH: The political alignment formed in Negri Sembilan may be extended to the upcoming Melaka state election, says Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan. He said the matter would be discussed at the Umno Supreme Council meeting on Aug 28, chaired by party president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. The deputy works minister said the meeting would consider the best strategy to secure a Barisan Nasional victory in Melaka.

items.title: Plans consented to by King for Gerak Khas must not be altered – Tunku Mahkota Ismail
items.summary: MERSING: All parties involved in planning the development of the Regimen Gerak Khas (RGK) have been reminded not to alter decisions that have received the consent of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for the benefit of certain parties. The Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, said that every plan and development involving the RGK must receive the consent of His Majesty, in his capacity as the Colonel Commandant of the RGK, and be carried out with the utmost trust and responsibility for the security and sovereignty of the nation. Tunku Ismail said the top leadership of the Defence Ministry, the armed forces and the army have a responsibility to ensure that the RGK's requirements, in terms of equipment, weaponry, mobility, technology, support systems and operational assets, are maintained at the highest level.

items.title: Jo Ghani: Malaysia’s LNG exports cushioning blow of Hormuz crisis
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 20 — Malaysia is better positioned to weather the fallout from the Strait of Hormuz disruption than nations solely dependent on imported energy, according to Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. “Actually, the Strait of Hormuz is more related to the energy sector. When the energy sector is affected, all industries will be affected,” he explained.

items.title: Dubai-based DP World expands Johor logistics footprint
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: DP World has opened an 11,514 square metres warehouse in Johor, strengthening its contract logistics capabilities and connectivity between Malaysia, Singapore and key regional trade corridors. DP World said the facility provides fast, secure and scalable warehousing and inbound logistics operations, strengthening its ability to deliver integrated supply chain solutions. Jeanie Tan, chief commercial officer of Asia Pacific logistics at DP World, said the Johor warehouse marks an important step in strengthening its growing logistics footprint across Southeast Asia.

items.title: West Kalimantan’s 4,000 hotspots likely to prolong haze in Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 20 — The ongoing haze in Sarawak is expected to persist as forest and land fires continue to rage in neighbouring West Kalimantan. According to a report by CNN Indonesia, Pontianak recorded the republic’s worst air quality on Thursday with an Air Quality Index (AQI) reading of 191 as of 6.56am local time, placing it in the ‘Unhealthy’ category. Besides Pontianak, several other areas in Indonesia also recorded ‘Unhealthy’ air quality on Thursday morning.

items.title: Haze forces two-day school closures in four Sarawak districts, home‑based learning activated
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 20 — The Sarawak Education Department has ordered schools in the Kuching, Padawan, Serian, and Samarahan districts under its supervision to close with immediate effect on August 20-21, due to the haze affecting air quality in these areas. “During the closure period, teaching and learning at home (PdPR) will be implemented to ensure continuity of students’ learning,” the statement read. As of 12 noon today, the Natural Resources and Environment Board (NREB) Daily Haze Watch recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in Serian (191), Kuching (188), and Samarahan (171).

items.title: Wife of Pantai Jerejak rep urges court to drop domestic violence case
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 20 — The wife of Pantai Jerejak assemblyman Fahmi Zainol has urged the Balik Pulau magistrates’ court to dismiss a case of voluntarily causing hurt against her husband. Nur Hidayah Abd Jabar told the court during the first day of the hearing today that she had withdrawn her initial police report and wished for the case to be dropped. Fahmi, 35, was charged with voluntarily causing hurt to Nur Hidayah, 35, at their home in Persiaran Pantai Jerejak 11, Bayan Lepas, at approximately 10pm on February 22.

items.title: Zambry: Higher Education Ministry unveils 2026-2030 plan to strengthen graduate employability
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — The Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) today launched the 2026-2030 Graduate Employability Strategic Plan (PSKG) to strengthen the country’s graduate employability ecosystem through a more comprehensive and integrated approach. “Therefore, we are implementing the Industry in Campus programme, particularly involving Malaysia’s technical universities and other universities such as Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM), research universities and other comprehensive universities,” he said. Zambry said the plan, anchored by the vision ‘Adaptive, Agile and Resilient Graduates as Catalysts for a High-Income Nation’, also involved cross-ministerial collaboration with the Economy Ministry, Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) and Human Resources Ministry (KESUMA).

items.title: Singaporean man and local youth claim trial over violent road rage brawl in Johor Bahru
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 20 — A 46-year-old Singaporean man claimed trial in the Sessions and Magistrates Court today on three charges, including obstructing police and possessing a dangerous weapon, following a violent confrontation last Sunday. Lim was charged under Section 6(1) of the Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Dangerous Weapons Act 1958, which carries a prison sentence of up to five years, and up to 10 years upon conviction. In separate proceedings, Lim also claimed trial before Magistrate Nurzihan Abdul Rehman to charges of obstructing a public servant and causing injury.

items.title: Fahmi calls for stronger online anti‑fraud outreach in rural areas amid rising cyber threats
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 20 — Awareness campaigns on online fraud or scams need to be strengthened and expanded to remote areas to protect rural communities from cyber threats that are increasing due to widespread internet access. He said this approach was important to provide direct exposure to the community, including sharing true stories from victims of online fraud. Commenting further, Fahmi said for the period from Jan 1 to yesterday, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had requested the removal of 476,516 online contents involving various categories of offences.

items.title: Man detained after viral video shows kitten hit with broomstick in Batu Gajah
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 20 — Police have detained a man after a video showing him abusing a kitten with an aluminium broomstick in a Batu Gajah housing area circulated on social media. Batu Gajah police district chief ACP Md Noor Aehawan Mohammad stated that the suspect surrendered himself at the Batu Gajah police headquarters after the footage went viral. The incident took place in the parking area of the suspect’s house,” Md Noor Aehawan said in a statement.

items.title: Immigration ‘Black Maria’ driver pleads not guilty to five charges over fatal Maju Junction crash that killed three
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — An Immigration Department ‘Black Maria’ lorry driver was charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with five offences, including dangerous driving that resulted in the deaths of a father and his two daughters here early yesterday. Mohd Akbar Zainol, 43, pleaded not guilty to all the charges, which were read out before Magistrate Aliaa Anwar. For the first to third charges, the accused was alleged to have driven the Isuzu lorry dangerously, resulting in the deaths of Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaikh Yahya, 53, and his two daughters, Siti Norshazlin, 24, and Siti Darwisyah Auni, 12, on Jalan Sultan Ismail at 1am on August 19.

items.title: Immigration suspends driver after fatal Maju Junction crash that killed three pedestrians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 20 — The Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM) has suspended the duties of the department’s lorry driver who was involved in a fatal accident that killed three family members at the Maju Junction traffic lights, Jalan Sultan Ismail here, yesterday. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the action was taken to enable authorities to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident. “Our department’s immediate action is to suspend the driver’s duties until the case is resolved and to provide full cooperation to the police in this case.

items.title: Perak MB’s political secretary resigns, cites health reasons amid drug allegations
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 20 — Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said his political secretary, Mohamad Hamidi Baharuddin, had resigned from his position, citing health reasons and the need to undergo medical treatment. Saarani said Hamidi had submitted his resignation letter dated August 10, stating that his resignation would take effect on August 17. Saarani was responding to a question on whether Hamidi’s resignation was linked to allegations of drug use that had been circulating on social media.

items.title: Johor Regent: Don’t alter Regimen Gerak Khas plans approved by the King
items.summary: MERSING, Aug 20 — All parties involved in planning the development of the Regimen Gerak Khas (RGK) have been reminded not to alter decisions that have received the consent of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for the benefit of certain parties. The Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, said that every plan and development involving the RGK must receive the consent of His Majesty, in his capacity as the Colonel Commandant of the RGK, and be carried out with the utmost trust and responsibility for the security and sovereignty of the nation. Tunku Ismail said the top leadership of the Ministry of Defence, MAF and the Malaysian Army has a responsibility to ensure that the RGK’s requirements, in terms of equipment, weaponry, mobility, technology, support systems and operational assets, are maintained at the highest level.

items.title: Telcos must explain alleged mass registration of phone lines under single identities by today, says Fahmi
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 20 — Telecommunications companies (telcos) must provide an immediate explanation over claims that a large number of telephone lines have been registered under individual identities and could be misused for online scams, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said his ministry would summon the telcos concerned and wanted their chief executive officers (CEOs) to provide a full explanation on the matter by the end of today. Earlier, Nadzim claimed that some telcos allowed between 20 and 50 telephone lines to be registered under a single name, raising concerns that the lines could be misused, including for online scams.

items.title: Johor police cripple drug ring, seize RM7.93m drugs from ‘repository’ homes
items.summary: Johor deputy police chief Hoo Chuan Huat said the first raid was at a house in Masai where police arrested three men, before seizing 39.809 kilogrammes (kg) of ecstasy powder suspected to be MDMA, 4.91kg of ketamine and 13,400 Erimin 5 psychedelic pills weighing 3.85kg. Police seized 230 cartridges of liquid suspected of syabu totaling 0.575 litres, 1.149kg of powder believed to be ecstasy and 358 grams of syabu. Hoo said the overall seizures involved 40.381kg of MDMA powder, 23.869kg of ecstasy powder, 23,025 Erimin 5 pills weighing 5.775kg, 574g of syabu, 4.91kg of ketamine, 18.4 litres of ketamine liquid and 0.575 litres of syabu liquid.

items.title: MyBorderPass down at KSAB bus and motorcycle lanes, travellers advised to switch to Immigration counters or MyNIISe
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 20 — The MyBorderPass application is experiencing a system access disruption at the entry and exit bus lanes as well as motorcycle lanes at the Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB) here today. The KSAB Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) said travellers affected by the disruption were advised to proceed to immigration counters or use the National Integrated Immigration System (MyNIISe) application for immigration clearance. MyBorderPass was launched and introduced by the Home Ministry (KDN) and the Immigration Department of Malaysia on Jan 1, 2025 as an initial digital initiative to facilitate immigration clearance using QR codes at the country’s main entry points.

items.title: KL-Karak expansion on track for early 2029 completion, says Nanta
items.summary: GOMBAK, Aug 20 — The RM2.1 billion Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway (KLK) expansion project, including a new 999-metre tunnel through Genting Sempah, is expected to be completed ahead of its 2030 target, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said today. Speaking after the groundbreaking ceremony for the third Genting Sempah tunnel and launch of the KLK widening project here, he said the project was expected to improve safety and convenience for motorists travelling between the Klang Valley and the east coast. “The project is 45.3km long and the tunnel is 999m long.

items.title: Johor police arrest five, open three investigation papers over upside-down flags
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 20 – Police have arrested five individuals, while three investigation papers opened following several recent cases involving the Malaysian flag and the Johor state flag being displayed upside-down in the state. Johor deputy police chief Hoo Chuan Huat said the arrests were from three reported cases that were under the Kulai, Iskandar Puteri and Johor Bahru South police jurisdictions. “So far, police have opened three investigation papers involving the three cases.
